title: Eviction Orchestrator for Predictive Maintenance and Throughput Guarantees
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a cluster-side 'Eviction Orchestrator' that automates node evacuation/draining, upgrade windows, and preemptive maintenance while preserving committed throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers. The controller must coordinate with the autoscaler, traffic router, and capacity-reservation service to ensure we meet per-customer SLOs and avoid cascading throttles during maintenance.

Scope:
- Controller that plans and executes node evacuations with awareness of model-level throughput reservations, active KV cache locality, and request latency SLOs.
- Policy engine for maintenance windows: rolling, canary, urgent maintenance, blackout windows, and customer-specified preferred windows.
- Integration points: Dedicated autoscaler (scale-out before drain), routing layer (drain-aware diversion to compatible variants), console APIs for scheduling, and telemetry hooks to surface impact.
- Draining strategies: fast-evacuate (for security/urgent patches), graceful-drain (for minimal throughput or stateful cache), and staged-drain (hybrid: spill + pre-warm nodes).
- Safety: enforce min-capacity reservations, runway checks, and automatic rollback if tail-latency or throughput drops exceed thresholds.

Out of scope for this ticket: per-tenant KV replication protocol changes, long-term capacity planning algorithm improvements (tracked separately).
comments: 2025-01-14 - Maya Chen: Initial spec drafted after on-call incident where a maintenance window caused 30% throughput regression for a high-commitment customer. Captured immediate requirements and risks.

2025-01-21 - Architecture sync: Decided to implement as a controller in the control plane (not on each node) to centralize decisioning and simplify sync with the autoscaler. Action: design detailed control loop and state machine.

2025-01-28 - Design review with Runtime and Autoscale teams: Agreed on model-aware eviction: controller will consult model placement table and attempt to co-locate KV cache warming paths before evicting nodes hosting hot model shards. Liam to prototype warming API in runtime. (Notes: design doc link added to attachments)

2025-02-05 - PM feedback (Sanjay Patel): Add a customer-visible 'maintenance impact preview' endpoint so teams can preview estimated throughput impact and suggested schedule. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-12 - Security review request submitted. Need to ensure maintenance API respects RBAC and audit logging for Private deployments. Assigned to Security for fast-track review.

2025-02-20 - Prototype results: Fast-evacuate reduces time-to-evict by 60% but increases tail latency for 3-5 minutes unless autoscaler pre-scales. Implementing preflight capacity check in controller (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/834).

2025-02-24 - QA note: Simulated mixed-tenant workload in staging. Observed a scenario where two concurrent maintenance jobs collided and created transient token throttles. Plan: add cross-job locking and capacity fencing. Liam to implement fencing in next patch.
2025-02-28 - Current: Branch opened for orchestration, integration tests added. Preparing canary rollout to internal Dedicated fleet next week behind feature flag 'eviction-orchestrator-v1'.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can schedule and execute a rolling drain for a Dedicated pool while maintaining committed throughput >= 95% of target in test harness for 95th percentile of customers.
Console API: customers can schedule maintenance, select preferred window, and preview estimated impact.
Safety gates: preflight capacity check, runway margin enforcement, cross-job fencing, and automatic rollback on SLO breach.
End-to-end integration tests exist that simulate urgent patch vs. planned maintenance and validate fallback behaviors.
RBAC and audit logs for maintenance actions are present for Private deployments.
